claims.claim: Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullianus was a Carthaginian Christian writer born around 155‑160 AD and died after 220 AD.
Tertullian wrote the treatise in answer to a personal query from his brother Fabius about whether Christians should flee persecution.
He argues that flight is forbidden because persecution comes from God’s will, and fleeing would constitute apostasy.
The work reflects the Montanist prophetic line, a stance that contrasts with his earlier, milder view expressed in De Patientia.
It addresses the contemporary controversy of whether Christians should avoid persecution by fleeing or by paying bribes, a practice common among believers at the time.
